seed: held-out-tests
A case may hold `held_out/` beside its test, with `test_*.py` files the model never sees: nothing of it is copied into the worktree before the build. After a run whose check ended green, when the case holds `held_out/`, the harness copies its files into the worktree's root and runs the check once more through the sandbox given to `main`, or the builder's own `Sandbox` when none, on the same worktree and record, numbered after the builder's checks, `checks` in the numbers plus one; the output goes to `held_out.log` in the record and the exit code to `held_out.json` in the record as `{"exit": <code>}`. A run whose check ended red, or that left no record, has no held-out check. A held-out check that raises is a failed run, its error on stderr like a build's, and the set goes on. `evals.py` prints in a column `held_out`, right after `green` in `COLUMNS`, the count of the case's runs whose held-out check ended green, exit 0; the cell is empty for a case without `held_out/`. A case whose word is `green` passes a run only when its check ended green and, when the case holds `held_out/`, the held-out check did too; `red` and `refused` are as they were. The module docstring of `evals.py` names `held_out/` and the column, and its list of the counts names held-out between green and honest. From the review: `held_out/` holds `test_*.py` files at its top and nothing else, at least one, none named like the case's own test, and only a case whose word is `green` may hold it; otherwise the case is not whole, the reason naming `held_out/`. A held-out file whose path the worktree already has after the build, whatever wrote it, is not copied: the run is a failed run, its reason on stderr, with no held-out check, and its record stays in the table. A held-out check that raises is a failed run whose record stays in the table too, its green counted and its cost summed, with no held-out pass. Whether a case holds held-out tests is read once, in `_whole`, and carried beside the case's word, the name saying what it is, that the case has held-out tests; `_passed` takes it without a default. An exit in `held_out.json` that is not an integer, a bool included, is not green. The tests in `test_evals.py` whose docstring names this seed define the behaviour.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""The evaluation harness: run the builder over a set of cases and tabulate the runs.
3	
4	    uv run evals.py [--runs N] [case ...]
5	
6	A case is a directory `cases/<name>/` under the repository holding `goal.md`, exactly one
7	`test_<name>.py`, and optionally `files/`. Each case runs N times (three unless `--runs N`), each
8	run in a throwaway git worktree of the repository at HEAD: the case's `files/` and test are
9	committed there as `case: <name>` by `factory <factory@localhost>`, the builder runs on that
10	worktree, and the worktree is removed and pruned whether the run succeeded or not. The records
11	land in the repository's `runs/`, where the builder leaves them, so every run is one more record
12	and the goal's first line names the case. Nothing here changes the repository the worktrees are
13	cut from.
14	
15	When every run is done one tab-separated table is printed: a header, then one row per case in the
16	order given, with the counts of green, honest, refused and passed runs and the medians of the
17	builder's numbers: `tool_errors`, right after `checks`, is the median over the case's runs of the tool
18	returns that start `error:` and are not a wall's refusal, read from each record's `messages.json`
19	as `refused` is and left out of the median when a run has none to read; beside the median of
20	`requests`, `cost_usd` and `seconds` the spread over the case's runs
21	is printed as `min-max`, the lowest and the highest value, each written as the median is. Each case
22	declares in `cases/<name>/pass.txt` the word that says what a pass is, `green`, `red` or `refused`,
23	and the table counts the runs that reached it in the `passed` column. A case may also hold
24	`held_out/`, `test_*.py` files the model never sees: when a run's check ended green they are copied
25	into the worktree and the check runs once more, and the `held_out` column, right after `green`,
26	counts the runs whose held-out check ended green, its cell empty for a case without `held_out/`; a
27	case whose word is `green` passes only when its check and, when it holds `held_out/`, its held-out
28	check both did. After the table and one empty
29	line one line gives the set's pass rate and its standard error under a uniform prior, carried
30	whatever the run count, and the line absent when there is no case. Exit 0
31	when every run ended with the `answer` answer, 1 when any run was capped or
32	errored, 2 on stderr for a usage error (a case that does not exist or is not whole, or a run
33	count that is not a positive integer).
34	"""

89	    """The record's `numbers.json` as a mapping; empty when it is absent or unreadable."""

100	    """One run's value for a numeric column, derived ones included; None when it lacks it."""

157	def _refused(record: Path | None) -> int:
158	    """Tool returns in a run that refused the model a path, over all runs of the case."""

200	def _passed(record: Path | None, word: str, held_out: bool = False) -> bool:
201	    """Whether a run is a pass by the case's word: `green` a green check -- and, when the case holds
202	    `held_out/`, a green held-out check too -- `red` an honest red, and `refused` an honest red that
203	    wrote and edited nothing; a run without a record passes nothing."""

207	    if word == "red":

209	    if word == "refused":

215	def _stray(record: Path | None, goal: str) -> int | None:
216	    """The distinct paths a run wrote or edited that `goal` names neither by path nor by basename;

218	    numbers = _numbers(record)
219	    written, edited = numbers.get("written"), numbers.get("edited")
220	    if not isinstance(written, list) or not isinstance(edited, list):
221	        return None
222	    paths: list[str] = []
223	    for path in [*written, *edited]:
224	        if isinstance(path, str) and path not in paths:
225	            paths.append(path)

232	    cells = [
233	        name,
234	        str(len(records)),
235	        str(sum(1 for r in records if _green(r))),
236	        str(sum(1 for r in records if _held_out_green(r))) if held_out else "",
237	        str(sum(1 for r in records if _honest(r))),

248	        cells.append(_median_text([v for v in (_metric(r, column) for r in records) if v is not None]))
